lead.t: There are three types, neurofibromatosis 1 (NF1), neurofibromatosis 2 (NF2), and schwannomatosis, all of which are clinically and genetically distinct diseases and should be considered separate entities.

snip.t: There are three types, neurofibromatosis 1 (NF1), neurofibromatosis 2 (NF2), and schwannomatosis, all of which are clinically and genetically distinct diseases and should be considered separate entities.
Café-au-lait macules (CALMs) are the hallmark of neurofibromatosis and are present in almost 100% of patients.
Neurofibromatosis type 2 have a high incidence of vestibular schwannomas that are frequently bilateral.
Neurofibromatosis type 1 is associated with an increased incidence of schwannomas of the spinal nerve roots.
Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is common in patients with multiple endocrine neoplasia 1 and rare with neurofibromatosis and tuberous sclerosis.
A solitary mass with no other lesions is unlikely to be part of neurofibromatosis.
Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1, chromosome 17): café-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, axillary freckling, optic gliomas, phaeochromocytoma (under 5%).

qs.q: Which of the following clinical features is considered the hallmark of neurofibromatosis type 1 and is present in almost 100% of patients?
qs.e: Café-au-lait macules are the hallmark of neurofibromatosis type 1 and are present in almost all patients. Lisch nodules and axillary freckling are also diagnostic criteria, but they appear later or at lower frequencies compared to café-au-lait macules.

qs.q: What minimum size criterion for café-au-lait macules applies to a postpubertal individual being evaluated for neurofibromatosis type 1?
qs.e: For postpubertal individuals, café-au-lait macules must be greater than 15 mm in greatest diameter to count toward the diagnostic criteria. In prepubertal individuals, the threshold is greater than 5 mm.

qs.q: At approximately what age does skinfold freckling (axillary or inguinal freckling) typically begin to appear in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1?
qs.e: Axillary or inguinal freckling usually appears between 3 and 5 years of age, reaching a frequency of over 80% by 6 years of age. It is one of the key diagnostic features of NF1.

qs.q: What is the most frequently observed central nervous system tumor in individuals with neurofibromatosis type 1?
qs.e: Optic gliomas are the most frequently observed CNS tumor in NF1, occurring in approximately 15 to 20% of affected individuals. Vestibular schwannomas are instead characteristic of neurofibromatosis type 2.

qs.q: A 4-year-old child with neurofibromatosis type 1 is found to have an optic pathway tumor extending into the hypothalamus. Which endocrine abnormality is this child at risk of developing?
qs.e: Extension of optic gliomas into the hypothalamus can lead to precocious puberty in children with NF1. Hypothyroidism and adrenal insufficiency are not specifically highlighted as direct consequences of hypothalamic extension in this context.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the inheritance pattern and genetic basis of neurofibromatosis type 1?
o: Autosomal dominant with loss-of-function NF1 mutations
X-linked dominant disorder with mutations in merlin
Autosomal recessive with a defect on chromosome 22
qs.e: NF1 is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in the NF1 gene located on chromosome 17q11.2. Chromosome 22 and the merlin gene are instead associated with neurofibromatosis type 2.

qs.q: Which of the following clinical features is typically required for the diagnosis of neurofibromatosis type 2?
qs.e: Bilateral vestibular schwannomas are a hallmark diagnostic criterion for neurofibromatosis type 2. Café-au-lait macules, freckling, and sphenoid dysplasia are classic features of neurofibromatosis type 1 rather than NF2.

qs.q: A 14-year-old boy with a family history of neurofibromatosis type 2 undergoes a slit-lamp examination to evaluate for characteristic ophthalmologic manifestations. Which of the following findings is most likely to be identified?
qs.e: Posterior subcapsular lens opacities occur in approximately half of patients with neurofibromatosis type 2 and serve as an early diagnostic clue. Iris Lisch nodules are specific to neurofibromatosis type 1 rather than type 2.

es.q: List and explain the diagnostic criteria for neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1).
es.m:
**Diagnostic criteria for NF1**
- Six or more café‑au‑lait macules (>5 mm pre‑pubertal, >15 mm post‑pubertal) – hallmark skin lesions present in almost all patients.
- Axillary or inguinal freckling (2–3 mm hyperpigmented macules) – appears between 3‑5 years, >80 % by age 6.
- Two or more iris Lisch nodules – hamartomas of the iris, seen in >74 % of NF1, prevalence rises with age.
- Two or more cutaneous neurofibromas or one plexiform neurofibroma – rubbery skin lesions; plexiform type may be congenital and cause overgrowth.

es.q: List the diagnostic features required for neurofibromatosis type 2 (NF2).
es.m:
**Diagnostic features for NF2**
- Bilateral vestibular schwannomas – pathognomonic for NF2.
- A first‑degree relative with NF2 plus either a unilateral vestibular schwannoma or any two of: meningioma, schwannoma, glioma, neurofibroma, or posterior subcapsular lenticular opacities.
- Unilateral vestibular schwannoma plus any two of: meningioma, schwannoma, glioma, neurofibroma, or posterior subcapsular lenticular opacities.
- Multiple meningiomas (≥2) plus a unilateral vestibular schwannoma or any two of: schwannoma, glioma, neurofibroma, or cataract.
